name: @civitai/blocks-react
description: React hooks and iframe transport for Civitai Apps. Pairs with @civitai/app-sdk/blocks.
comment-peerDependencies: The @civitai/app-sdk floor is DERIVED, not chosen: it is the lowest published
version that exports every symbol this package imports from the peer.
🔴 RAISED 0.40.0 -> 0.45.0 when this package began importing two NEW peer VALUE
symbols -- `boundBlockToParentMessageType` and `OTHER_MESSAGE_TYPE_LABEL`, used by
`internal/iframeTransport.ts` to bound the `BLOCK_MESSAGE_REJECTED` label. Both
ship for the first time in the app-sdk minor released alongside this change, so
0.45.0 is not a margin: it is the first version that has them. Measured against
the then-latest published 0.44.0 -- which SATISFIED the old range -- both are
absent from every subpath, and the failure is not a type error: `dist/index.js`
re-exports `IframeTransport`, so the package's MAIN ENTRY is in the failing module
graph and the block does not boot at all. Caught by an adversarial audit that
built the dist and resolved it, not by any gate; the paragraph below says why no
gate can. Step 4's positive control was run (a symbol that cannot exist reported
as absent), so the zero for the other symbols is a measurement and not a silent
pass.
⚠️ 0.45.0 IS A PREDICTION ABOUT RELEASE ORDERING, NOT A MEASURED VERSION. It is
what the pending minor changeset publishes ONCE THIS BRANCH IS ON TOP OF a main
where app-sdk is already 0.44.0 and the catalog changeset has been consumed. If
another minor releases FIRST, the two symbols ship in 0.46.0 while 0.45.0
publishes WITHOUT them and SATISFIES this range -- #309's shape exactly, the one
this floor exists to close.
🔴 AND `changeset version` WILL REWRITE THIS RANGE DOWNWARD IF IT RUNS TOO EARLY.
An earlier revision of this note said onlyUpdatePeerDependentsWhenOutOfRange
'guarantees changeset version will not correct it'. That is BACKWARDS, and it is
measured: run on this branch as it stands (app-sdk 0.43.0 in-tree, the catalog
changeset still present, so app-sdk computes to 0.44.0), `changeset version`
rewrites `>=0.45.0 <1.0.0` to `>=0.44.0` -- it LOWERS the floor to the exact
version that lacks the symbols AND drops the upper bound. The flag rewrites a
peer range precisely when the computed version falls OUT of it. Post-merge it
computes 0.45.0 and leaves the range alone, which is why this is not a live
defect -- but never run `changeset version` on this branch before rebasing, and
re-read the range afterwards rather than trusting the flag to protect it.
🔴 A PEER RANGE IS METADATA AND NOTHING CHECKS IT AGAINST THE CODE. 0.49.0-0.51.0
declared >=0.29.0 while importing `effectiveBrowsingCeiling` (app-sdk 0.39.0) and
the create-post types (0.40.0). The range was SATISFIED, so no install warned;
the failure landed at module evaluation in a consumer's tests, where 27 of 43
test files collected ZERO tests -- 292 tests stopped running and the summary line
reported no failures. See #309. CI cannot catch this: `pnpm.overrides` maps the
peer to the workspace copy, so every in-repo typecheck is blind to whatever this
range says.
🔴 AND #309'S OWN SUGGESTED FLOOR (>=0.39.0) WAS WRONG. `effectiveBrowsingCeiling`
arrives in 0.39.0, but `BlockCreatePostRequest`, `BlockCreatePostResult`,
`BlockCreatePostHostError` and `BlockPostSource` arrive in 0.40.0, and there is no
0.39.x patch between them. Landing the issue's number would have closed it and
stayed broken. Do not take a floor from a ticket.
TO RE-DERIVE IT (do this when this package starts importing a new peer symbol):
1. collect the symbols -- every named `import`/`export … from '@civitai/app-sdk*'`
clause in src/, plus bare and star forms, which name a SUBPATH and no symbols
but still have to resolve. At the time of writing: 62 symbols, 2 subpaths
('/blocks' and '/safe-storage').
2. in a scratch dir OUTSIDE this workspace (pnpm would resolve the peer to the
workspace copy and measure nothing), `npm i @civitai/app-sdk@<version>` and
typecheck a file importing all of them -- each in the POSITION it is imported
in here, since a type-only export satisfies a plain value import and that is
the #309 failure mode itself.
3. the floor is the lowest version with zero missing. Confirm the version BELOW
it is missing something, or the floor is higher than it needs to be.
4. include a symbol you know does not exist, and check it reports. A run that
finds nothing is indistinguishable from one wired to nothing.
A 584-line script that automated this was written and then cut: three audit rounds
found defects in the SCRIPT while the floor value it derived never changed, and
nothing in the repo ran it. The derivation is rare and the number is recorded here;
the tool was the expensive half.
